bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_1: A line of Fluid Pipes links the containers at its ends, two or as many as you like
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_2: Right-clicking a straight piece with a Wrench adds a window to it
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_3: A windowed piece stays straight: pipes placed beside it will not join it
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_4: A Mechanical Pump driven by rotation makes the fluid travel through the pipes
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_5: Right after starting, nothing is taken out of the source yet
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_6: As soon as the flow reaches the far end, the contents move over little by little
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_flow.text_7: The pipes only guide the transfer: no fluid is ever stored inside them
bearing.guide.fluid_pipe_interaction.tex: Each open end of a pipe network can work with the block placed in front of it
Anything that stores fluid can be emptied or filled this way
An open end sitting on a source block drinks it up...
...and an open end facing empty space pours out new sources
A few other blocks, such as cauldrons, can also be drained by pipes directly
bearing.guide.encased_fluid_pipe.text_1: Fluid Pipes can be covered with Copper Casing
bearing.guide.encased_fluid_pipe.text_2: Besides hiding the pipe, the casing fixes its openings exactly as they are
bearing.guide.encased_fluid_pipe.text_3: A pipe placed next to it no longer makes it open a new side...
bearing.guide.encased_fluid_pipe.text_4: ...and removing a neighbour does not close one either
bearing.guide.mechanical_pump_flow.text_: A Mechanical Pump decides how fluid moves in the pipes connected to it
The arrow on its body shows which way the fluid is pushed
The side behind the pump is now the intake...
...and the side in front is the outlet
Turning the input the other way does not change the pump direction
To send the fluid the other way, right-click the pump with a Wrench
bearing.guide.mechanical_pump_speed.head: Pump Speed and Reach
bearing.guide.mechanical_pump_speed.text: No matter how fast it turns, a pump reaches pipes up to 16 blocks away
With a faster input, the flow spreads through the pipes sooner...
Several pumps on the same network add up their throughput
They must all point the same way, though
bearing.guide.valve_pipe.text_1: A Fluid Valve can stop or release the flow inside a pipe line
bearing.guide.valve_pipe.text_2: Whether it lets fluid pass depends on the rotation given to its shaft
bearing.guide.valve_pipe.text_3: Turned in the opening direction, the valve opens and the fluid flows on
bearing.guide.valve_pipe.text_4: Turning it the other way shuts it again
bearing.guide.smart_pipe.text_1: Smart Fluid Pipes let fluids through depending on what kind they are
bearing.guide.smart_pipe.text_2: Right next to a source, they choose which fluid gets pulled out of it
bearing.guide.smart_pipe.text_3: To set it, Right-click the filter slot holding a container of that fluid
bearing.guide.smart_pipe.text_4: Further down a line, it acts as a gate that passes only the matching fluid
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_storage.text_1: A Fluid Tank is a bulk store for liquids
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_storage.text_2: Pipes may fill or empty them through any of their faces
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_storage.text_3: A Comparator reads how full the tank is
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_storage.text_4: Survival players cannot use buckets on a tank directly
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_storage.text_5: To move fluid in or out of items, use Basins, Item Drains or Spouts
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_sizes.header: How Big a Tank Can Get
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_sizes.text_1: Tanks placed together merge into one larger tank with more room
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_sizes.text_2: The footprint of a tank can be as wide as 3 by 3 blocks...
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_sizes.text_3: ...while its height can stack up past 30 layers
bearing.guide.fluid_tank_sizes.text_4: A Wrench toggles whether a tank shows its window
bearing.guide.creative_fluid_tank.text_1: A Creative Fluid Tank is an endless source of one fluid
bearing.guide.creative_fluid_tank.text_2: Right-click it with an item holding a fluid to pick which one it supplies
bearing.guide.creative_fluid_tank.text_3: Pipes can draw that fluid from it for ever, it never runs dry
bearing.guide.creative_fluid_tank.text_4: Whatever is pumped back into it simply disappears
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.header: Flooding and Emptying Areas with a Hose Pulley
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_1: Hose Pulleys are for flooding or emptying wide areas of fluid
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_2: Rotation fed into it lowers its hose to the wanted depth
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_3: With the rotation reversed, the hose is wound back up
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_4: Pipes attach to the side opposite its front
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_5: Pipes can push fluid down the hose so the pool rises...
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_6: ...or suck it back up so the pool sinks
bearing.guide.hose_pulley.text_7: How quickly the pulley fills or drains depends only on what the pipe network can move
bearing.guide.hose_pulley_level.text_1: With the hose fully reeled in, the pulley has nothing to work with
bearing.guide.hose_pulley_level.text_2: Draining takes away the uppermost layer first
bearing.guide.hose_pulley_level.text_3: It stops once the surface sits one layer below the end of the hose
bearing.guide.hose_pulley_level.text_4: Filling starts at the bottom and works its way up
bearing.guide.hose_pulley_level.text_5: The pool never rises higher than one layer above the hose end
bearing.guide.hose_pulley_infinite.text_: Lower the hose into a big enough body of water, like an ocean...
...and it hands out or takes in fluid while the water stays exactly as it was
Pipe networks can pull from or push into such a pulley without limit
bearing.guide.spout_filling.header: Pouring into Items with a Spout
bearing.guide.spout_filling.text_1: A Spout pours fluid into items that are put underneath it
bearing.guide.spout_filling.text_2: You cannot pour fluid into a Spout or take any out by hand
bearing.guide.spout_filling.text_4: A Depot under the Spout is one way to hold the items being filled
bearing.guide.spout_filling.text_5: Items riding a belt below it...
bearing.guide.spout_filling.text_6: ...the Spout stops each one, fills it and lets it move on by itself
bearing.guide.item_drain.header: Emptying Items in an Item Drain
bearing.guide.item_drain.text_1: An Item Drain empties out the fluid that items carry
bearing.guide.item_drain.text_2: Right-click with a filled item to empty it into the drain
bearing.guide.item_drain.text_4: ...roll over it and leave their fluid behind on the way
bearing.guide.item_drain.text_5: Pipes can then draw the collected fluid out of the drain
bearing.guide.portable_fluid_interface.t: Pipes have no way to reach the Fluid Tanks of a moving contraption
This interface lets you reach them, and the contraption need not be stopped for it
Put a second one where the first will pass, leaving a gap of 1 or 2 blocks
When one passes the other, the two link up
Once linked, the fixed interface gives access to all tanks on board
Fluid can be pumped into it...
Once nothing has been moved for a little while, the contraption carries on
bearing.guide.pulse_extender.text_1: A Pulse Extender makes a signal that runs through it last longer
bearing.guide.pulse_extender.text_2: It turns on shortly after receiving the signal...
bearing.guide.pulse_extender.text_3: ...and only turns off again once the set time has run out
bearing.guide.pulse_extender.text_4: Scroll on the value panel to choose how long the output is held
bearing.guide.pulse_extender.text_5: The time can be set anywhere up to a full hour
bearing.guide.pulse_repeater.text_1: After a delay, a Pulse Repeater sends out one brief pulse
bearing.guide.pulse_repeater.text_2: The delay before the pulse is set by scrolling on the value panel
bearing.guide.pulse_repeater.text_3: Delays as long as one hour are possible
bearing.guide.powered_latch.text_1: A Powered Latch works like a lever that redstone can flip
bearing.guide.powered_latch.text_2: A signal reaching its back turns it on, and it stays on
bearing.guide.powered_latch.text_3: A signal coming from the side turns it off again
bearing.guide.powered_latch.text_4: You can also flip it yourself with a right-click
bearing.guide.powered_toggle_latch.text_: Think of it as a lever that a redstone pulse can flip
Each signal arriving at its back switches it to the other state...
...so it goes on, then off with the next one
A right-click toggles it by hand as well
bearing.guide.analog_lever.text_1: Analog Levers give out an exact amount of redstone power from a single block
bearing.guide.analog_lever.text_2: Each right-click raises its output strength by one
bearing.guide.analog_lever.text_3: Sneak while right-clicking to lower it step by step
bearing.guide.nixie_tube.header: Numbers and Text on Nixie Tubes
bearing.guide.nixie_tube.text_1: Given a redstone signal, Nixie Tubes show its strength as a number
bearing.guide.nixie_tube.text_2: Right-click with a written Clipboard to show your own text on them
bearing.guide.nixie_tube.text_3: Dye applied with a right-click changes the colour the tubes glow
bearing.guide.redstone_link.text_1: Redstone Links relay power between two points with nothing in between
bearing.guide.redstone_link.text_2: Sneak-right-clicking turns a link into a receiver
bearing.guide.redstone_link.text_3: A Wrench does the same job with a plain right-click
bearing.guide.redstone_link.text_4: A receiver outputs whatever power a transmitter within 256 blocks sends
bearing.guide.redstone_link.text_5: Items put into its two slots set the frequency it uses
bearing.guide.redstone_link.text_6: Links only talk to each other when their frequencies are the same
bearing.guide.rose_quartz_lamp.text_1: A redstone signal switches a Rose Quartz Lamp on
bearing.guide.rose_quartz_lamp.text_2: Even after the signal is gone, it keeps putting out redstone power
bearing.guide.rose_quartz_lamp.text_3: Lamps placed side by side form a group...
bearing.guide.rose_quartz_lamp.text_4: ...and turning one of them on moves the signal there, switching the rest off
bearing.guide.rose_quartz_lamp.text_5: A Comparator measures how far away the lit lamp of the group is
bearing.guide.rose_quartz_lamp.text_6: A Wrench can also switch a lamp on or off by hand
bearing.guide.pulse_timer.text_1: Pulse Timers keep sending out brief pulses, one after another
bearing.guide.pulse_timer.text_2: Scroll on the value panel to change the time between pulses
bearing.guide.pulse_timer.text_3: Powering its input side pauses the timer and starts its count over
bearing.guide.pulse_timer.text_4: Invert the output by right-clicking the bottom plate of the circuit
bearing.guide.pulse_timer.text_5: That is handy for machines that only run while they are not powered
